Modified assessment with SLOOS lens: Cautiously positive, nudged higher. The June 16, 2021 FOMC statement emphasizes strong activity and employment gains under very accommodative policy. SLOOS corroborates improving credit supply: banks eased standards for residential real estate (including GSE-eligible mortgages and HELOCs) and key consumer categories (credit cards, autos), lowered minimum credit score requirements, and eased C&I terms for investment‑grade firms—supporting transmission of policy and the flow of credit. Offsetting this, standards in several categories remain tighter than pre‑pandemic, some banks report tighter policies on select C&I exposures, and foreign banks kept standards unchanged for IG borrowers while tightening for below‑investment‑grade firms; CRE underwriting remains cautious. Net effect: improving credit availability reinforces the positive tone but persistent pockets of tightness keep it guarded.
